'''''Ornithogalum dubium''''', [[common name]]s '''sun star''', '''star of Bethlehem'''<ref name = RHSPF/> '''orange star''',<ref>Sabine Fillinger and Yigal Elad, eds., ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=ACk3CwAAQBAJ&pg=PA464 Botrytis – the Fungus, the Pathogen and its Management in Agricultural Systems]'' (2015), p. 464.</ref> or '''yellow chincherinchee''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asparagaceae]], subfamily [[Scilloideae]]. It is a South African (Cape Province) [[endemism|endemic]].

The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''dubium'' means "dubious" or "unlike others of the genus".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref>

==Description==
Growing to {{convert|50|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall, ''O. dubium'' is a [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant|perennial]] with 3-8 yellowish green leaves. The leaf margins are ciliate with scapes {{convert|10|-|25|cm|0|abbr=on}} long. The flowers are borne in winter or spring, in cylindrical to almost spherical racemes consisting of 5-25 flowers. The [[tepal]]s may be orange, red, yellow or rarely white, often with a green or brown center.
The common name of the genus Ornithogalum, Star-of-Bethlehem, is based on its star-shaped flowers, after the [[Star of Bethlehem]] that appeared in the biblical account of the [[birth of Jesus]]. The genus Ornithogalum contains about 180 species.

==Cultivation==
[[File:PikiWiki Israel 42304 Plants of Israel.JPG|thumb|right|250px|Ornithogalum dubium commercially grown in Israel]]
''O. dubium'' is frost-tender and is best overwintered in a dry, frost-free place, then re-potted in spring. The main soil requirement is excellent drainage, with ample water early in the growth cycle, but dry during the dormant season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Southern African Ornithogalum |url=http://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/SouthernAfricanOrnithogalum |publisher=Pacific Bulb Society|accessdate=17 July 2013}}</ref> The plant should be grown in a sheltered spot in full sun. It is reported to be toxic by ingestion, and the leaves cause irritation.<ref name = RHSPF/> 

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Ornithogalum dubium'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/115215/Ornithogalum-dubium/Details | accessdate=15 April 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 70 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 14 April 2018}}</ref>
